paragraphs.source_en:
(‘ “Stay, Adonis; hapless Adonis, stay, that for the last time I may possess thee, that I may
fold thee in my arms and mingle lips with lips. Awake, Adonis, for a little space, and give
me one last kiss again. Kiss me so long as life is in the kiss, until thy spirit has passed into
my lips, thy breath flowed into my heart, and I have drained thy sweet love-philtre and
drunk up thy love; and I shall guard that kiss as though it were Adonis’ self, since thou,
hapless one, art flying from me. Far away thou fliest, Adonis, and comest to Acheron, to
a grim king and a cruel.” ’)
S. clearly recalls his own translation of part of this passage (Longman ii 697–700, no. 201) ll. 40–8:
